_comment: The TRADE / EXCHANGE EVALUATOR, Layer B of the decision-substrate roadmap (docs/LAYERS_RESEARCH.md), composed ON the value field (Layer A) and env-gated SWEG_TRADE_EVAL, default OFF, a no-op unless SWEG_VALUE_MOVE=1 is also set, byte-identical when unset. This is an ARTIFICIAL-INTELLIGENCE PILOTING HEURISTIC, NOT a Warhammer 40,000 10th-edition game rule — there is no codex or core rule that tells a player which objective marker to commit to when weighing what the commitment trades. Following the precedent of simulator.target_economics, simulator.threat_projection_charge and simulator.value_projection (all explicitly-flagged AI design heuristics), this entry quotes the core wound-roll-and-save and 2D6 charge wording the exchange's expected-wounds and reach math is built from, and cites the real-play TRADING doctrine that motivates it: a competent player prices a commitment by what dies on BOTH sides — what the unit removes from its best reachable target next activation against what the enemy's reply removes from it — and trades UP (a cheaper body into a dearer one) rather than committing to valuable ground it cannot pay for. THE GAP this layer closes: the value field (simulator.value_projection) prices a destination's DESTINATION VALUE and RISK, but not the EXCHANGE — a unit commits to a marker without asking what it kills from there versus what kills it over the following turn, so trade-poor armies over-commit and trade-rich armies under-punish. The mechanic does not change combat math or draw any new random number — it only re-points the value consumer's objective argmax by adding the symmetric one-ply exchange as a TILT, and it never freezes a claim or contest (it re-targets among objective destinations only; the settled blanket-charge-block rejection, SWEG_AM_CHARGE_DISCIPLINE at minus 2.41, is respected).

simulator.trade_exchange.rule_name: Wound roll (Strength vs Toughness) + Saving throw / invulnerable save + Charge roll (2D6) (10e Core Rules) — one-ply symmetric trade-exchange piloting heuristic
simulator.trade_exchange.quoted_text: If the Strength characteristic of the weapon used is equal to the Toughness characteristic of the target model's unit, a Wound roll of 4+ is required... for each of those attacks that successfully wounded the target unit, the player commanding that unit can attempt a saving throw... if that unit has an invulnerable save, the player can use that instead of their normal saving throw... To make a charge roll, roll 2D6. The unit can make a Charge move if the result is greater than or equal to the distance (in inches) between it and the closest enemy unit it wishes to charge.
simulator.trade_exchange.trigger: SWEG_TRADE_EVAL=1 (default off; a no-op unless SWEG_VALUE_MOVE=1 is also set, and byte-identical when unset). In strategy.py pick_move_intent, for each candidate objective destination already ranked by the value field's net score net(p) = V(p) - unit_future_value * frac_at_risk(p), add the symmetric one-ply exchange EXCHANGE(p) = OUR RETURN(p) - THEIR REPLY(p), then re-argmax. OUR RETURN(p) is the value the moving unit expects to remove from its single BEST reachable enemy target by shooting or charging from p next activation: for each living enemy E, the ranged expected wounds (simulator._ranged_expected_wounds — shots, hit fraction, Strength-vs-Toughness wound fraction raised to any matching Anti-X floor, the unsaved fraction after armour or invulnerable save, damage per shot) when p is within the unit's Move + weapon range, OR the melee expected wounds (strategy._kill_potential_wounds) times the exact 2D6 charge-reach probability (strategy._p_2d6_at_least) after the unit's Move, whichever is larger, capped at E's remaining wounds and priced points-per-wound (E's points_cost / starting wounds) times the value field's relevance ((5 * scoring_rounds_remaining) / a documented reference points constant, victory points per point over the rounds remaining); the maximum over enemies is OUR RETURN (a unit commits to one target). THEIR REPLY(p) is the incoming threat field T at p (strategy._threat_field_at, the SAME field simulator.value_projection already computes, summed over every LIVING enemy with the audited expected-wounds per-pair math and the positional Benefit-of-Cover tax), priced as the unit's expected REMAINING value at stake: the death probability min(1, T / max(1, remaining wounds)) — the SAME survival ratio the value field's tolerance term uses (strategy.value_projection frac_at_risk) — times the unit's FULL points_cost, with NO relevance discount; a unit's death is a full-price loss regardless of what the square was worth, so only the RETURN (the opportunity side of the exchange) carries the relevance weighting (the version-two reply pricing, re-specified from first principles after the version-one symmetric relevance-discounted reply measurably under-deterred realized exposure — the walked-into-it falsifier rate rose under trade — and after the intermediate raw-points-per-wound candidate was measured still insufficient for damaged units); for a MOVE destination T_post equals T because moving onto a marker commits no single enemy's death. No new random number is drawn; the per-round threat-field projector cache (strategy._threat_projectors) is reused; co-committed friendly units are deliberately deferred (in-flight friendly move intents are not cleanly readable at this point).
simulator.trade_exchange.effect: AI move-intent destination-selection heuristic (Layer B, composed on Layer A's value field). The value consumer's objective argmax over net(p) is re-taken over net(p) + EXCHANGE(p), a TILT that prices what the commitment TRADES: a marker from which the unit can remove more value from a crackable enemy than the enemy's reply removes from it scores higher, and a marker whose reply out-prices the return scores lower, so trade-poor armies stop over-committing to valuable ground they cannot pay for and trade-rich armies punish where the exchange is positive. The pricing is points-proportional: the RETURN is points-per-wound times the value field's relevance, which is what makes trading UP — a cheap body into a dear one — read as the value gain it is (the reference points constant is set so the AVERAGE committed unit's full trade dual equals the value field's flat per-unit dual, continuity with Layer A, and is documented as a reference, not a tuned knob); the REPLY is the unit's death probability (the tolerance term's survival ratio, min(1, T / max(1, remaining wounds))) times its FULL points_cost with NO relevance discount (version two — a death is a full-price loss, and a damaged body sees its whole remaining value at stake; the discounted version-one reply under-deterred realized exposure per the walked-into-it falsifier, and the raw points-per-wound intermediate candidate was measured still insufficient). It is a TILT, never a hard veto: it only re-points the argmax among already-legal objective destinations, it never freezes a claim or contest into a hold (the settled blanket-charge-block rejection SWEG_AM_CHARGE_DISCIPLINE at minus 2.41 is respected — re-target, never freeze), and it only acts when SWEG_VALUE_MOVE=1 (with the value gate unset the whole value block never runs, so SWEG_TRADE_EVAL=1 alone is byte-identical). This is an AI design heuristic, not a 10e rule — the quoted core wound-roll, saving-throw and 2D6 charge-roll wording is the combat math the exchange's expected-wounds and reach figures are built from; it alters no dice, roll, or damage value, and it draws no new random number. Faithful and even-handed: it fires for ALL factions and both armies consult it (the substrate escape from the closed-matrix wash). HONEST CAVEAT (inherited from simulator.value_projection and simulator.threat_projection_charge): the ranged expected wounds on both sides of the exchange are attenuated only by the angle-independent positional cover the sim's shooting RESOLUTION enforces, not by line-of-sight occlusion — the exchange plans with the geometry the resolution applies.

_trade_doctrine_reference: Real-play doctrine motivating this heuristic, presented as doctrine (not a rules citation) per the same disclosure pattern as the _threat_range_doctrine_reference note in data/rule_citations.d/threat_layer.json and the _value_field_doctrine_reference note in data/rule_citations.d/value_layer.json: trading is named one of the cornerstones of a game whose goal is to remove your opponent's assets — a good trade kills enough to cover its cost or trades UP and kills more than what you paid for, and at the army scale every unit is expendable so the army trades pieces efficiently, spending a body where sacrificing it denies the opponent scoring or gains an objective. Sources: https://www.belloflostsouls.net/2025/12/warhammer-40k-tactics-understanding-trades-baits-bricks.html (understanding trades, baits and bricks: trading up) and https://www.goonhammer.com/unit-roles-in-9th-edition-attrition/ (attrition role: every unit expendable, trade pieces efficiently), both cited in docs/LAYERS_RESEARCH.md Layer B for exactly this trade-evaluator concept.
